applicant_utility.summary: No scholarship literally titled 'Kyushu University International Scholarship' is currently published on Kyushu University's own site; the scheme that matches its description (tuition borne by the university, monthly stipend, round-trip airfare for outstanding international graduate students) is the MEXT scholarship as recommended by Kyushu University. Apply through the Student Affairs Office of your target graduate school rather than contacting MEXT directly, and confirm that graduate school's internal window because dates differ by school. Note that Kyushu's published monthly figure for master's students (147,000 yen) is higher than the FY2027 MEXT guideline figure (144,000 yen), so budget against the current guidelines, not the university's page. Privately financed students who cannot get a national scholarship should email the International Student Exchange Division (intlr-pscholar@jimu.kyushu-u.ac.jp) for private-foundation options and expect to need Japanese for most of them.

official.deadline_note: There is no single central deadline: the call for applications opens at each Japanese diplomatic mission around mid-April of the previous year and the deadline for submission of application documents varies according to each Japanese diplomatic mission; confirm the deadline at the mission's website in your country of nationality
official.application_cycle: FY2027 intake, arrival in Japan in April 2027 or September/October 2027; recruitment between April and May of the previous year (April-May 2026 for this cycle)
official.status_note: The 2027 cycle application window at each Japanese diplomatic mission (around mid-April to May 2026, mission-specific deadlines) has passed; embassy first screening ran from around early May to late July 2026 and final results for this cycle are notified from January to early March 2027. The next intake follows the same April-to-May recruitment window in 2027, with deadlines set again by each mission
official.tuition_coverage_note: MEXT publishes: 'Fees for the entrance examination, matriculation, and tuition at universities are waivered.' The entrance examination fee, however, will be borne by the grantee if the student cannot proceed to the master's or doctoral course or cannot be admitted to the university
benefits: Allowance: 143,000 yen per month for students receiving preparatory education and non-regular (research) students; 144,000 yen per month for regular students enrolled in master's or professional degree courses; 145,000 yen per month for regular students enrolled in doctoral courses
Supplemental regional allowance of 2,000 or 3,000 yen per month added for grantees studying or conducting research in specially designated regions
Education fees: fees for the entrance examination, matriculation, and tuition at universities are waivered

Traveling expenses: economy-class airline ticket from the grantee's country of nationality to an international airport in Japan used on the normal route to the accepting university, and return at the end of the scholarship period
Scholarship payment may be suspended for an extended absence from the university, and MEXT reserves the right to change amounts each fiscal year due to the Japanese Government's budget situation
eligibility: Applicants must have the nationality of a country that has diplomatic relations with Japan and must not hold Japanese nationality at the time of application (dual nationals may apply only if they relinquish Japanese nationality by arrival in Japan)

Age: applicants, in principle, must have been born on or after April 2, 1992; exceptions are limited to circumstances of the applicant's country such as military service obligation or loss of educational opportunities due to war

Academic background: 16 years of school education outside Japan (or equivalent) for a master's course; an overseas master's-equivalent degree or two or more years of recognised research for a doctoral course; 18 years for medicine, dentistry, veterinary sciences and certain pharmaceutical fields
Applicants must be willing to learn Japanese, be interested in Japan, and have the ability to conduct research and adapt to living in Japan
Applicants must submit a health certificate in the prescribed format signed by a physician
Applicants must choose the April 2027 arrival period (arrive between April 1 and April 7, 2027) or the October 2027 period and cannot change it in principle after submission
Applicants must newly obtain a 'Student' visa from the Japanese diplomatic mission in their country of nationality before travelling to Japan
requirements: Applications must be submitted to the Japanese embassy or consulate general in the country of the applicant's nationality; documents must not be sent directly to MEXT
Applicants must apply for the field of study they majored in at university or a related field; the field may be restricted by the Japanese diplomatic mission in the applicant's country

Applicants who pass the First Screening must contact Japanese universities directly to request letters of provisional acceptance, in the MEXT-specified format, with no more than two universities contacted at the same time and a maximum of two letters
An application may be rejected if it arouses weapons proliferation concerns, including those over weapons of mass destruction and related items

Grantees must enrol in National Health Insurance upon arrival in Japan and are recommended to bring at least approximately US$2,000 to cover immediate living expenses because the first payment comes one to one-and-a-half months after arrival
documents: Placement Preference Application Form for FY2027
Field of Study and Research Plan (FY2027 form)
Academic transcript for all academic years of university attended
Certification of graduation or degree certificate of the university attended (or certificate of prospective graduation if not yet graduated)
Recommendation letter from the president/dean or the academic advisor at the current or last university attended (free format)
Medical certificate (Certificate of Health on the FY2027 form, filled in by a professional medical doctor)
Abstracts of theses, if the applicant has written theses
Certificate of language proficiency (Japanese or English), only if held, issued no earlier than two years before the application date, three copies
Recommendation letter from the present employer, if currently employed
Photographs of works of art or recorded musical performance, if majoring in fine arts or music
selection_criteria: First Screening by the Japanese diplomatic mission: examination of submitted documents, written examinations of Japanese and English language proficiency, and an interview
Document screening must show academic achievement at the last university equal to or above a certain level and a detailed, concrete research plan

The interview must reveal a clear sense of purpose about studying in Japan, information-gathering about Japanese universities, and sufficient Japanese or English to communicate with the academic advisor
A letter of provisional acceptance greatly influences final selection results; applicants without one may be rejected
Second Screening and university placement by MEXT based on the First Screening results and placement preferences
coverage: Monthly allowance of 143,000 yen (non-regular/research students), 144,000 yen (master's) or 145,000 yen (doctoral), plus a 2,000-3,000 yen monthly supplemental regional allowance where applicable
Waiver of entrance examination, matriculation and tuition fees
Economy-class round-trip airfare between the country of nationality and Japan on the normal route
application_method: Read the Application Guidelines for Research Students and follow the instructions
Complete the FY2027 Application Form, Placement Preference Application Form, Field of Study and Research Plan, Certificate of Health and Recommendation Letter
Submit the documents to the Japanese embassy or consulate general in your country of nationality by its deadline; do not send documents to MEXT

After passing the First Screening, contact up to two prospective universities directly after notification (for the 2027 cycle, contacts from September 2, 2026 were not permitted) to obtain letters of provisional acceptance in the MEXT-specified format, and submit the final Placement Preference Application Form to the mission by its deadline
Await MEXT Second Screening and university placement; results are notified via the diplomatic mission from January 2027 to early March 2027
official.application_route: Apply through the Japanese embassy or consulate-general in your country of nationality; MEXT must not be contacted directly
official.citizenship_residency: Must hold the nationality of a country with diplomatic relations with Japan and not hold Japanese nationality at application; dual nationals must relinquish Japanese nationality by arrival
official.international_eligibility: Open to nationals of countries with diplomatic relations with Japan; the First Screening must be conducted at the mission of the chosen nationality
official.subject_or_agency_requirement: Applicants should apply for the field they majored in at university or a related field; traditional entertainment arts and subjects requiring practical training at factories or companies are excluded; medical, dentistry and welfare students cannot engage in clinical training without the relevant Japanese licence
official.research_requirement: Applicants apply as Research Students to conduct research in a specialised field at a Japanese graduate school, university institute or similar, with a Field of Study and Research Plan that serves as an important reference for university placement
official.duration: Non-regular students: April 2027 to the end of March 2029 (April arrival) or September/October 2027 to the end of March 2029 (October arrival), with the first 6 months devoted to Japanese-language preparatory education where required. Regular students: the standard period of study of the relevant course, plus a possible 6-month preparatory period
official.description: The MEXT Scholarship Embassy Recommendation for Research Students is the Japanese government scholarship in which candidates apply through their national Japanese embassy or consulate general, which conducts the first screening (documents, written Japanese and English examinations, and an interview), before MEXT conducts the second screening and university placement for arrival in April 2027 or September/October 2027.
official.program_type: Government scholarship (Ministry of Education, Culture, Sports, Science and Technology, Japan) - Embassy Recommendation, Research Students
official.english_requirement: First Screening includes a written English examination taken by all applicants alongside a written Japanese examination; the English test may be exempted for countries where English is the official language. A certificate of English or Japanese language proficiency is submitted only if the applicant holds one, and it must be issued no earlier than two years before the application date

applicant_utility.summary: For the 2027 intake the embassy-route application window (April-May 2026, exact date set by each mission) has already closed, so plan for the next cycle, which opens around April of the intake's preceding year. You apply only through your national Japanese embassy or consulate general, and the two gates that sink most applicants are failing the embassy's written Japanese and English examinations plus interview, and arriving at the provisional-acceptance stage without a supervisor's letter. After passing first screening you must secure up to two letters of provisional acceptance directly from universities within a narrow, fixed window, because MEXT places you at a university that has already issued one and rejects applicants without any. Budget roughly US$2,000 in cash for the first weeks, since the first stipend instalment arrives one to one-and-a-half months after arrival and is paid only into a Japan Post Bank account.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Recent graduates under the age limit with a master's-level research plan who can secure a Japanese university supervisor and pass embassy-level Japanese and English exams
application_readiness_checklist: Confirm the exact application deadline at the website of the Japanese embassy or consulate general in your country of nationality well before the cycle opens
Prepare the research plan around the field you majored in, since it drives university placement
Book the embassy's written Japanese and English examinations and interview preparation early; both language exams are compulsory unless English is exempted for your country
Have the Certificate of Health completed by a registered physician, not a general practitioner formality, and keep language certificates within the two-year validity window
Research prospective supervisors in advance so you can contact universities immediately after passing first screening, and use the MEXT-specified letter format
common_rejection_risks: Failing to obtain any letter of provisional acceptance, which leads to rejection at MEXT's second screening
Contacting universities before the permitted window or more than two universities at once, or pressing universities to issue letters early
Holding Japanese dual nationality without a firm plan to relinquish it before arrival
Being currently enrolled or planning to enrol at a Japanese university as a privately financed student
Planning to receive another scholarship from the Japanese government or a government-related organisation
Submitting the Certificate of Health not completed by a professional medical doctor, or art/music applicants omitting required work samples
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Domestic travel from home to the nearest international airport, airport taxes and usage fees, in-Japan travel, travel insurance, carry-on and unaccompanied baggage expenses, accommodation and all living costs beyond the monthly allowance, and National Health Insurance premiums
document_audit: Documents must be in Japanese or English or carry a Japanese/English translation
Number every document from 1 to 11 in the upper right corner of its first page
The arrival period (April or October) cannot in principle be changed after submitting the application form
Language proficiency certificates must be issued within two years of the application date, and three copies are required
Submitted documents are not returned, and bound documents may be dismantled during review
alerts: Age cutoff for this cycle is being born on or after April 2, 1992; exceptions are limited to country-level circumstances, never personal ones
A previous MEXT scholarship makes you ineligible unless three or more years have passed and specific programme exclusions apply
Applicants without a letter of provisional acceptance may still submit the Placement Preference form but are restricted to the October term
MEXT reserves the right to change or cancel arrival dates, scholarship amounts and guideline contents under unavoidable circumstances, and the amount may change each fiscal year
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Submit documents to the national Japanese embassy or consulate general, pass document/language exam/interview first screening, obtain provisional acceptance letters directly from up to two universities, MEXT second screening and placement, results via the mission January to early March 2027
